examples.ko: 공사장 앞에 레미콘 트럭이 줄지어 서 있어요.
examples.en: Concrete mixer trucks are lined up in front of the construction site.

examples.ko: 레미콘이 도착하자 일꾼들이 서둘러 바닥에 부었어요.
examples.en: When the ready-mix concrete arrived, the workers hurried to pour it on the floor.
The driver of the concrete truck from the site asked me for directions.

examples.ko: 아침에 레미콘이 여러 대 지나가서 도로가 막혔어요.
examples.en: Several concrete trucks passed this morning, so the road was blocked.

examples.ko: 건물을 지으려면 레미콘이 아주 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: To build a building, you need a lot of ready-mix concrete.

examples.ko: 이 근처에는 레미콘 공장이 있어서 트럭이 자주 다녀요.
examples.en: There's a ready-mix plant near here, so trucks pass often.

explain: 공장에서 미리 반죽해서 트럭으로 실어 오는 콘크리트를 말해요. 그 콘크리트를 싣고 다니는 트럭도 그냥 '레미콘'이라고 부르는 일이 많아요. 건설 현장이나 도로 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: A big concrete mixer truck passed by.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콘크리트를 싣고 다니는 트럭을 정확히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the truck that carries the concrete.

phrases.en: There is a ready-mix concrete plant near my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콘크리트를 만드는 공장을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the plant where the concrete is made.

phrases.en: The workers poured concrete on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사 현장에서 콘크리트를 쏟아 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at a building site for pouring concrete.

explain_en: It means concrete that is mixed at a plant beforehand and delivered by truck. The truck that carries it is also often just called '레미콘'. You hear it at construction sites and in road news.

en: emergency working; being on emergency duty; emergency operation

examples.en: Because of the typhoon, we go on emergency duty from today.
The fire station staff were on emergency duty all night.

examples.ko: 비상근무 기간에는 휴가를 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't take vacation during the emergency duty period.

examples.ko: 명절 연휴에도 비상근무 중인 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people are on emergency duty even over the holiday.

examples.ko: 폭설 예보가 나오자 시청이 비상근무 체제로 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: When heavy snow was forecast, city hall switched to an emergency duty system.

examples.ko: 남편이 비상근무라서 오늘 집에 못 와요.
examples.en: My husband is on emergency duty, so he can't come home today.

explain: 재난이나 사고에 대비해 평소와 다르게 모두 출근하거나 대기할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '비상근무에 들어가다', '비상근무 체제'라는 표현을 자주 볼 수 있어요. 평소에 하는 '야근'과는 달리 상황 때문에 정해진 근무라는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: City Hall went on emergency duty because of the heavy snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비상근무를 시작할 때 쓰는 뉴스에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase common in the news for starting emergency duty.

phrases.en: The hospital is now on an emergency duty system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비상근무로 운영되는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the state of operating under emergency duty.

phrases.en: The staff are on emergency duty right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중'을 붙여 지금 하고 있다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 중 means it is happening right now.

explain_en: It is used when everyone reports to work or stands by differently from usual to prepare for a disaster or accident. In the news you will often see '비상근무에 들어가다' and '비상근무 체제'. Unlike ordinary overtime ('야근'), it is a duty set up because of the situation.

examples.en: The fishing boats stopped operating because of the typhoon.
The sea is rough today, so fishing is difficult.
My father works on a boat that fishes far out at sea.

examples.ko: 불황 때문에 공장이 조업 시간을 줄였어요.
examples.en: Because of the slump, the factory cut its operating hours.

examples.ko: 날씨가 좋아지면 내일부터 조업을 다시 시작해요.
examples.en: If the weather improves, we will start fishing again from tomorrow.

examples.ko: 이 바다에서는 겨울에 조업 금지 기간이 있어요.
examples.en: In this sea, there is a period in winter when fishing is banned.

explain: 뉴스에서 '조업 중단', '조업 금지'처럼 한 덩어리로 자주 나와요. 고기잡이배에는 '조업하다', 공장에는 '가동하다'도 많이 써요. '제조업'과는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: Fishing boats work at sea from dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조업'을 동사로 쓴 말로, 고기잡이배가 일하는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 조업, used for fishing boats at work.

phrases.en: Fishing is banned in this sea during winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 안내문에 자주 나오는 한 덩어리 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase that often appears in news and notices.

phrases.en: The weather improved, so the fishing boats resumed operations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멈췄던 일을 다시 시작한다는 뜻으로 '조업 중단'의 반대 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting again what had been stopped, the opposite of 조업 중단.

explain_en: Operating work at sea or a plant, like fishing or factory production. In the news it often appears as a set phrase, such as '조업 중단' (work stoppage) or '조업 금지' (fishing ban). For fishing boats people say '조업하다', and for factories '가동하다' is also common. It is a different word from '제조업' (manufacturing), so do not mix them up.

examples.en: Cargo handling continued all night at the port.

examples.ko: 파업 때문에 하역이 늦어져서 물건이 안 들어와요.
examples.en: Because of the strike, unloading is delayed and the goods aren't arriving.

examples.ko: 하역 시간이 길어지면 비용이 더 들어요.
examples.en: If the unloading time gets longer, it costs more.
A large ship takes as long as two days to unload.
The dock workers started working from dawn.
The weather was bad, so we put off the unloading until tomorrow.

explain: 주로 배나 항구에서 짐을 내리고 싣는 일을 말하고, 뉴스에서는 '항만 하역', '하역 작업'처럼 나와요. 물류 현장에서는 짐을 싣고 내리는 일을 '상하차'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The truck arrived at the unloading area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐을 싣고 내리는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where cargo is loaded and unloaded.

phrases.en: The dock workers start working at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 항구나 창고에서 짐을 옮기는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: People who move cargo at ports or warehouses.

phrases.en: Unloading costs went up, so prices rose too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐을 싣고 내리는 데 드는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The cost of loading and unloading cargo.

explain_en: It mainly refers to loading and unloading cargo at ships and ports, and the news uses it in phrases like '항만 하역' and '하역 작업'. In logistics work, loading and unloading is also called '상하차'.

en: to flicker; to blink; to glimmer

examples.en: I am sleepy, so my vision keeps going hazy.
The lighthouse light is faintly flickering in the distance.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 기억이 가물거려서 확실히 말을 못 하겠어요.
examples.en: My childhood memories are hazy, so I cannot say for sure.
The candle flickered in the wind and then went out.
Grandpa says his memory is getting hazy these days.
The street lamps look dim and flickering in the fog.

explain: 불빛이 꺼질 듯 말 듯하거나 기억, 시야가 흐릿해질 때 써요. '깜빡거리다'가 빠르게 켜졌다 꺼지는 느낌이라면, 이 말은 희미해져 가는 느낌이 강해요. 사람이 주어이면 '정신이 가물거리다'처럼 의식이 흐려진다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: It was in my childhood, so my memory is hazy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억이 희미해서 잘 생각나지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a memory is faint and hard to recall.

phrases.en: The pain was so bad that I nearly lost consciousness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의식이 흐려질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when consciousness is fading.

phrases.en: I can see a flickering light far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 올 때 쓰는 '-는' 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-neun' form used before a noun.

explain_en: Faint, wavering light about to go out (촛불이 가물거리다) It is used when a light seems about to go out, or when memory or vision grows blurry. '깜빡거리다' feels like quickly turning on and off, while this word feels more like fading away. It can also describe a fading mind, as in '정신이 가물거리다'.

t90.ax: I am sleepy, so my vision keeps going hazy.

examples.en: Snowfall is expected in the central region tomorrow.
All flights were cancelled because of the snowfall.
The roads froze from the snow, and there were many accidents.
The sudden snowfall paralyzed the morning commute.
This winter's first snowfall came at the end of November.

examples.ko: 시에서는 강설을 대비해 제설 작업을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The city began snow-clearing work in preparation for snowfall.

explain: 일상에서는 '눈이 오다'라고 말하고, '강설'은 일기 예보나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 비가 내리는 '강우'와 짝으로 같이 말하기도 해요. 눈이 오는 양은 보통 '적설량'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This winter's snowfall is greater than last year's.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 내린 양을 말할 때 쓰는 말로, 일기 예보에서 많이 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the amount of snow that fell; often heard in weather forecasts.

phrases.en: Snowfall is expected across the country this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 눈이 올 것이라는 예보를 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to report a forecast that snow will fall.

phrases.en: The road was jammed because of the snowfall, so I was late to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈 때문에 차가 많이 밀리는 문제를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain traffic problems caused by snow.

explain_en: In daily life people say '눈이 오다'; '강설' is mostly heard in weather forecasts and news. It pairs with '강우' (rainfall). The depth of accumulated snow is usually called '적설량'.

examples.en: In midwinter the river freezes over completely.
Ice fishing starts only after the lake has frozen.
The temperature dropped overnight and the road froze.
The temperature at which water freezes is zero degrees.

examples.ko: 항구가 결빙하면 배가 다닐 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the port freezes over, ships cannot run.
As the weather warms up, the pond that had frozen is melting.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '얼다', '얼어붙다'를 많이 쓰고, '결빙하다'는 딱딱한 글이나 설명에서 나와요. 도로 안내의 '결빙 구간'처럼 명사로 더 자주 보이고, 반대말은 '해빙'이에요.

phrases.en: Please drive slowly in icy sections.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도로 안내에서 얼음이 어는 길을 가리키는 말로 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use is in road signs for sections where ice forms.

phrases.en: The road froze overnight and is slippery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 얼어붙은 상태를 말할 때 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal word for something that has frozen over by itself.

phrases.en: It's so cold that the river froze solid.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결빙하다'보다 입말에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word used much more in everyday speech than '결빙하다'.

explain_en: Written/technical — water surface freezes over (호수가 결빙하다) In everyday talk people say '얼다' or '얼어붙다', while '결빙하다' appears in formal writing and explanations. It is seen more often as a noun, as in '결빙 구간' (icy section) on road notices, and the opposite is '해빙'.

t90.ax: If the port freezes over, ships cannot run.

examples.ko: 여름에 음식을 오래 두면 구더기가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you leave food out for long in summer, maggots appear.
I was shocked to see maggots in the trash can.
There was a terrible smell because of the maggots.
Maggots are the larvae of flies.

examples.ko: 이제 구더기도 없고 냄새도 안 나서 다행이에요.
examples.en: Thankfully, there are no maggots and no smell anymore.
My friend ran away, scared by the maggots.

explain: 파리의 애벌레로, 음식물 쓰레기나 상한 음식에 생겨서 징그러운 느낌이 강해요. 속담 '구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까'에도 나와서 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 조금 힘들 수 있어도 해야 할 일은 해야지, 구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까요?
phrases.en: It might be a bit hard, but we have to do what needs doing; we can't stop just because of a little trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방해가 될 일이 있다고 해서 꼭 필요한 일을 포기하면 안 된다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning you shouldn't give up something necessary just because of possible trouble.
phrases.en_equiv: You can't make an omelette without breaking eggs.

explain_en: These are fly larvae that appear in food waste or spoiled food, and the word feels disgusting. It also appears in the proverb '구더기 무서워 장 못 담글까', which is worth knowing.

examples.ko: 강원도 산간 지역에 대설 특보가 발효됐어요.
examples.en: A heavy snow warning has been issued for the mountainous areas of Gangwon Province.
The expressway was closed because of the heavy snow.

examples.ko: 올해 첫 대설로 출근길이 많이 막혔어요.
examples.en: The first heavy snow of the year caused heavy traffic on the morning commute.
Heavy snow is expected tomorrow, so leave early.
After a heavy snowfall, the roads freeze and get slippery.
Daeseol, one of the 24 solar terms, falls around early December.

explain: 눈이 많이 내리는 것을 말하고, 24절기 중 하나의 이름이기도 해요. 일기예보에서는 '대설주의보', '대설경보'처럼 자주 보여요. 갑자기 쏟아지는 눈은 '폭설'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: A heavy snow advisory was issued this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기예보에서 가장 자주 만나는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in weather forecasts.

phrases.en: A heavy snow warning was issued, so school is closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주의보보다 더 심각한 단계의 특보예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more serious alert level than the advisory.

phrases.en: The roads were blocked because of yesterday's heavy snowfall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 쏟아지는 눈을 말하고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to sudden, intense snowfall and is more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It means a large amount of snowfall, and it is also the name of one of the 24 solar terms. In weather forecasts you see it in '대설주의보' and '대설경보'. A sudden heavy snowfall is also called '폭설'.

t90.ax: Heavy snow is expected tomorrow, so leave early.

examples.en: The sky flashed and then there was a loud thunderclap.
Every time the lightning flashed, the child was startled.
The camera flash went off and dazzled my eyes.
I closed my eyes at the sudden flash of light.
After it flashed outside the window, the power went out.

examples.ko: 손전등이 한 번 번쩍한 뒤에 꺼졌어요.
examples.en: The flashlight flashed once and then went out.

explain: 큰 빛이 한 번 잠깐 나타났다 사라질 때 써요. 번개나 카메라 플래시가 대표적이에요. 빛이 계속 반짝이는 것은 '번쩍거리다', '반짝이다'가 더 자연스러워요. 소리와 모양이 비슷한 '번쩍 들다'의 '번쩍'은 빠르게 들어 올리는 모습을 나타내는 부사예요.

phrases.en: snap awake; come to one's senses
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸리거나 멍하던 머리가 갑자기 또렷해질 때 써요. 충격을 받아 현실을 깨달을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sleepy or dazed mind suddenly becomes sharp, or when a shock makes you realize reality.

explain_en: It is used when a big light appears for just a moment and disappears, like lightning or a camera flash. For light that keeps sparkling, '번쩍거리다' or '반짝이다' is more natural. The '번쩍' in '번쩍 들다' is a separate adverb describing something being lifted quickly.

examples.ko: 고기를 구울 때 불똥이 튀어서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Sparks flew while I was grilling meat, and I was startled.
Sparks flew up into the sky from the campfire.

examples.ko: 용접할 때는 불똥이 튀니까 보호 안경을 써야 해요.
examples.en: Sparks fly when welding, so you must wear protective glasses.

examples.ko: 촛불 심지에 불똥이 앉으면 불빛이 어두워져요.
examples.en: When a burnt bit forms on the candle wick, the light gets dimmer.

examples.ko: 팀장님 실수 때문에 우리한테까지 불똥이 튀었어요.
examples.en: Because of the team leader's mistake, we got dragged into it too.

examples.ko: 그 싸움의 불똥이 튈까 봐 멀리 피했어요.
examples.en: I stayed far away, afraid of getting caught up in that fight.

explain: '불꽃'이 타오르는 불의 모양이라면 '불똥'은 튀어 오르는 작은 불 조각이에요. 일상에서는 '불똥이 튀다'라는 비유로 특히 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 팀장님 실수 때문에 우리한테까지 불똥이 튀었어요.
phrases.en: Because of the team leader's mistake, we got dragged into it too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 한 일이 아닌데 다른 사람의 잘못이나 문제의 나쁜 영향이 나한테까지 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the bad effects of someone else's mistake or trouble reach you even though you did nothing.

explain_en: Small bit of fire that jumps off, like from a campfire. While '불꽃' is the shape of a burning flame, '불똥' is a small bit of fire that flies off. In daily life it is especially common in the figurative phrase '불똥이 튀다'.

examples.en: Flies are buzzing around the food.
A motorcycle roared out of the alley.
The machines at the construction site droned all day.
Honeybees fly around among the flowers, buzzing.

examples.ko: 선풍기가 붕붕대는 소리 때문에 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The humming of the fan woke me up.

examples.ko: 모기가 귀 옆에서 붕붕대서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: A mosquito buzzed next to my ear, and it made me angry.

explain: '붕붕거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. '-대다'는 소리나 행동이 계속 반복되는 느낌을 줘요. 벌레나 기계의 소리를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: A bee is buzzing around the flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '붕붕대다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 붕붕대다 and can replace it.

phrases.example: 밤에 파리가 붕붕대는 소리 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't sleep because of the buzzing sound of a fly at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 '소리'를 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는' lets it describe the noun 소리 (sound).

phrases.example: 창문 밖에서 파리가 하루 종일 붕붕댔어요.
phrases.en: A fly buzzed outside the window all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나간 일을 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the past tense, used for something that already happened.

explain_en: It means the same as '붕붕거리다' and can be swapped with it. The '-대다' ending gives a feeling of a sound or action repeating again and again. Use it for the sounds of insects and machines.

t90.ax: Flies are buzzing around the food.

examples.en: Suddenly a downpour poured down, and my umbrella was useless.
The game continued even in the pouring rain.

examples.ko: 밤새 내린 장대비 때문에 길이 물에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: The road was flooded because of the downpour that fell all night.
I ran home through the pouring rain.
When the downpour stopped, the sky cleared up.
They say it will pour heavily in the afternoon.

explain: 장대처럼 굵고 세차게 내리는 비를 말해요. '장대비가 쏟아지다/내리다'로 자주 쓰고, 뉴스의 '폭우'보다 구어적이에요. 잠깐 내리는 '소나기'와 달리 비의 굵기와 세기를 강조해요.

phrases.en: Torrential rain poured all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쏟아지다'보다 비가 세차게 계속 오는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a stronger sense of rain falling fiercely and continuously than '쏟아지다'.

phrases.en: I got drenched in heavy rain on the way home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우산 없이 굵은 비를 맞는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when being caught in heavy rain without an umbrella.

phrases.en: The road was blocked because of the heavy rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장대비'와 비슷하지만 뉴스나 안내에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 장대비 but used more in news and announcements.

explain_en: It refers to rain that falls thick and hard, like poles. It is often used as '장대비가 쏟아지다/내리다' and is more colloquial than the news word '폭우'. Unlike a short '소나기', it stresses the thickness and strength of the rain.

examples.en: When it rains, the yard turns into mud.

examples.ko: 우리는 장화를 신고 진창길을 겨우 걸었어요.
examples.en: We wore rain boots and barely made our way along the muddy road.

examples.ko: 신발이 진창에 푹 빠져서 꺼내기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: My shoe sank deep into the mud and was hard to pull out.

examples.ko: 공사장 앞은 진창이라서 조심해서 가야 해요.
examples.en: It's muddy in front of the construction site, so you have to go carefully.
The rice-field path turned to mire because of the rain.

examples.ko: 차 바퀴가 진창 속에 빠져 움직이지 않았어요.
examples.en: The car's wheels were stuck in the mire and wouldn't move.

explain: 비가 온 뒤 질척질척해진 땅이나 길을 말해요. '진흙'은 흙 자체이고 '진창'은 그런 흙 때문에 질퍽해진 곳이에요. '진흙탕'이라고도 해요. '엉망진창'에도 들어 있지만, 혼자 쓰면 땅의 상태를 말해요.

phrases.en: The playground turned into a mud pit because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '진창'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 진창 and more common in speech.

phrases.en: The car wheel got stuck in the mud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질퍽한 땅에 발이나 차가 들어가 움직이기 어려울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a foot or vehicle sinks into soggy ground and gets stuck.
phrases.en_equiv: to get stuck in the mud

phrases.en: I stepped in the mud, so my shoes got dirty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비 온 뒤 질척한 길을 걷다가 신발이 더러워졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you walk on a soggy road after rain and your shoes get dirty.

explain_en: It means ground or a road that has become soggy and sticky after rain. '진흙' is the mud itself, while '진창' is the place made squelchy by it. People also say '진흙탕'. It appears inside '엉망진창' too, but on its own it describes the state of the ground.

t90.ax: When it rains, the yard turns into mud.
